tools.name: ask_yonatan
tools.description: Use this when a user asks about Yonatan Gross specifically (his work, projects, services, availability, or fit). Returns a grounded answer as text from the same model that powers the site chat.

tools.name: browse_projects
tools.description: Use this when a user asks what Yonatan has built or wants proof of production AI experience with a given stack. Returns his portfolio projects, each with a name, a one-line description and a link.

tools.name: book_intro_call
tools.description: Use this when a user wants to book a free 15-minute intro call with Yonatan to scope a build or discuss consulting. It books for real, in three calls: (1) with no slot it returns up to 5 free slots; (2) with slot, name and email it re-checks the slot and returns needs_confirmation with a confirm_tok

tools.name: list_intro_slots
tools.description: Use this when the booking view needs every open intro-call time. It returns the open start times of the next two weeks grouped by local day, with the server clock and the booking page link. For the app only: a model uses book_intro_call.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: book_intro_call · Private data: book_intro_call · Public sink: book_intro_call.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: book_intro_call · Private data: book_intro_call · Public sink: book_intro_call

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
